preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (address 0xE44d394BB296739739617497aaD26c9117A43c77)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call withdrawAllToOwner() function to drain all BUSD tokens accumulated from fees in the contract. This function swaps all accumulated IMPERIAL tokens for BUSD and sends them directly to the owner's specified receiver address. No other user interaction is required beyond the owner calling this privileged function.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has owner-only functions that allow draining funds. The owner is fixed at address 0xE44d394BB296739739617497aaD26c9117A43c77. By impersonating this owner, we can call withdrawAllToOwner() to swap all IMF tokens in the contract for BUSD and send them to our address.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the owner address and call withdrawAllToOwner() with attacker address as parameter to drain BUSD from the contract.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner address (0xE44d394BB296739739617497aaD26c9117A43c77)
2. Call withdrawAllToOwner(attacker) on the target contract
3. This will swap all IMF tokens in the contract for BUSD and send to attacker
4. Verify attacker's BUSD balance increased

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract holds BUSD tokens that are distributed to token holders via claim(). The owner has all IMF tokens initially. By impersonating the owner, we can transfer IMF tokens to ourselves, then claim BUSD rewards.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner to transfer IMF tokens to attacker. 2. Warp time forward 1+ hour. 3. Call claim() to receive BUSD rewards.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Impersonate owner address
2. Transfer IMF tokens from owner to attacker
3. Warp time forward by 1+ hour (3600+ seconds)
4. Call claim() as attacker to receive BUSD
5. Verify BUSD balance increased
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because withdrawAllToOwner() requires IMF tokens to be deposited in the contract from fees. Since no trading occurred, there were no fees. We need to first get IMF tokens and then claim BUSD rewards.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The owner can set fee receivers via setFeeReceivers(). By setting all fee receivers to attacker address, any trading fees (in BUSD) will go directly to attacker. This is a direct privilege abuse.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Get BUSD to trade. 2. Impersonate owner to set all fee receivers to attacker. 3. Buy IMF tokens to generate buy fees. 4. Sell IMF tokens to generate sell fees. All fees in BUSD go directly to attacker.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Use deal() to give attacker BUSD
2. Impersonate owner to setFeeReceivers(attacker, attacker, attacker)
3. Approve router to spend BUSD
4. Buy IMF tokens via router (generates fees to attacker)
5. Sell IMF tokens via router (generates more fees to attacker)
6. Verify attacker BUSD balance increased
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because the contract had no BUSD to distribute. The claim() function distributes BUSD that accumulates from trading fees. We need to first generate trading fees by buying/selling IMF tokens.
